title: Session 52 Failure Category Analysis — Classified by Rubric Impact
source: Session 52 audit findings re-analyzed against CERTIFICATION_RUBRICS.md §2

findings.learner_text: Explanation correctly states 'ASC 350-20' — only metadata field is wrong
findings.rubric_impact: NONE — AccountingPrinciple is not a rubric-gated field. D1 (accuracy) is unaffected: the correct standard IS applied in the learner-facing explanation.

findings.finding: 44 cases have ProductionStatus: 'Draft' despite all items being question_state: 'Certified'
findings.rubric_impact: NONE. D4 defect gate 'ProductionStatus → question_state contradiction' covers Production+Unprocessed (inflated claim), not Draft+Certified (conservative direction). No dimension cap.

findings.finding: 4 cases missing CompanyName metadata field (company IS named in ScenarioText)
findings.rubric_impact: NONE. CompanyName is optional per QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD.md. D4 Score 4 critical fields = 'CaseID, Title, SectionTags, Difficulty/DifficultyScore, ProductionStatus, Version' — CompanyName not listed. D2 satisfied by ScenarioText.

findings.finding: 305 items have item-level ProductionStatus: 'Draft' (case_items, not the wrapper)
findings.rubric_impact: NONE. CERTIFICATION_RUBRICS.md gates on case-level ProductionStatus. Item-level ProductionStatus is not a rubric dimension field.
NONE. Same reasoning as M-002 — optional field, ScenarioText is correct.

findings.finding: CBQ2-A3 BlueprintObjectives mentions 'Inventory valuation' but case tests revenue/ADA
findings.rubric_impact: D2 Score 4 requires 'Specific topic mapping.' One mismatched objective in an otherwise aligned case → minor. D2 likely remains ≥ 4.

findings.finding: CURRENT_BASELINES.md §2 table stale (Pack A shown as 481, actual 500)
findings.rubric_impact: NONE — documentation staleness, not a content defect.

findings.finding: 21 cases have generic Stakeholder: 'Management' instead of named role
findings.rubric_impact: BLOCKS. D2 Score 3: 'Company named but scenario is generic.' D2 requires ≥ 4 for certification. CAQS §3.1 requires 'a specific decision-maker with a role.' 'Management' is a collective noun, not a specific stakeholder. D2=3 in affected cases.

BLOCKS on cases with 2+ thin items. D5 Score 3: 'Explanations are correct but terse — state the answer without full reasoning.' Cases with 2+ such items fall at D5=3 < required 4. Cases with exactly 1 thin item may pass under Score 4 'Minor gaps' clause.

findings.finding: 34 cases have ExhibitCount < 2 — only 1 exhibit per case
findings.rubric_impact: NONE. No rubric dimension gate explicitly caps on exhibit count. D4 gate on ExhibitCount only fires when count field ≠ actual array length, not when count=1 correctly. CAQS §3.4 recommends ≥2 but rubric does not enforce.

findings.finding: Generic scenario language in some Draft cases (textbook-style vs. business-authentic)
findings.rubric_impact: D2 Score 3 for affected cases: 'Adequate but generic.' D2 minimum 4 → BLOCK. However, this was not quantified precisely in Session 52 — ad-hoc observation. Requires per-case D2 scoring.
findings.blocks_certification: YELLOW — depends on per-case D2 scoring

presentation.blocks_certification: PARTIAL — stakeholders + thin explanations block; exhibit count does not

findings.finding: 17 cases have uniform difficulty labels (all items same level) — DL-032
findings.rubric_impact: NONE. D6 defect gate 'No cognitive progression (all items same type/difficulty)' requires BOTH same type AND same difficulty. If item types vary (numeric→select→multi), uniform difficulty alone does not trigger this gate. D4 CF4 (DifficultyScore within ±1 of mean) passes trivially. No dimension cap.
NONE. CAQS §6.1 is a target distribution — not a rubric dimension or defect gate. The rubric gates on DifficultyScore PRESENCE, not distribution alignment.

findings.finding: 51 items with case-level DifficultyScore > 1 from item mean (CF4 violation)
findings.rubric_impact: D4 caps at 3 when CF4 violated. However, this requires per-case verification of which 51 items and whether the containing cases' D4 drops below 4. May affect a subset of cases.
D6 evaluates cognitive-level progression but not individual Bloom's mislabeling. No specific gate for mislabeled Bloom's level. D2 may be affected if LOSTag mismatches.

calibration.blocks_certification: MINIMAL — only CF4 violation cases potentially affected

findings.finding: 48 cases have cognitive progression violations — items not ordered Apply→Analyze→Evaluate
findings.rubric_impact: BLOCKS. D6 Score 3: 'Items don't follow cognitive progression.' Score 4: 'Items mostly follow progression but one pair is inverted.' When the entire sequence is unordered (template artifact), D6=3 < required 4. CERTIFICATION_RUBRICS.md defect gate also fires if items are all same type+same difficulty but independent gate.

findings.finding: Item type distribution not matching Gold Standard pattern (e.g., too many select, too few numeric)
findings.rubric_impact: NONE. Gold Standard type distribution is aspirational (CASE_STUDY_GOLD_STANDARD.md), not rubric-gated. D6 evaluates progression quality, not type-count targets.

findings.finding: Case-level QuestionCount/ExhibitCount fields present but may not equal array lengths (CF: cross-field rule)
findings.rubric_impact: D4 caps at 2 (QuestionCount≠Items.length) or 3 (ExhibitCount≠Exhibits.length). However, these are structural fields that were populated correctly during the S916 reconsolidation. Requires verification but likely clean.

findings.finding: 5 legacy scored_cases*.js files in repository root — governance violation (Constitution §11.4)
findings.rubric_impact: NONE — file hygiene, not a case content defect.

block_breakdown: Thin explanations → D5=3 (subset of 27 items across cases)
summary.most_impactful_single_finding: Cognitive progression (48 cases, 64% of inventory) — the only finding that independently blocks a large portion of the case pool under the certification rubric
summary.least_relevant_to_certification: Difficulty calibration (DL-032) and ExhibitCount < 2 — Session 52's heaviest-scored dimensions but have zero rubric gate impact
summary.key_insight: Session 52's 0/75 result is an artifact of the scoring instrument. When judged against the authoritative CERTIFICATION_RUBRICS.md, many cases would certify that Session 52 rated CONDITIONAL — specifically cases with proper cognitive progression, named stakeholders, and substantive explanations, regardless of their difficulty labels, exhibit count, or metadata completeness.
